articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like world places than the real category.
Tanganyika pushed me in that direction immediately.
Baikal kept that theory alive for a moment, but titicaca still did not quite fit.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then Titicaca made me stop thinking about world places and start thinking about the real category.
Tanganyika made sense as Lake Tanganyika.
Baikal made sense as Lake Baikal.
The answer was Names of lakes.
Geneva and Titicaca then felt less surprising and more like the last pieces falling into place.
Looking back, the answer feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: I first read Tanganyika and Baikal too literally and drifted toward world places. Tanganyika could be read as "Lake Tanganyika", while Baikal could be read as "Lake Baikal", so the board still felt open instead of solved.

Titicaca changed the direction because "Lake Titicaca" gave me a testable phrase, not just a loose topic. Once that line worked, I had a fixed place to put the repeated word and could go back through the earlier clues with a clearer target.

I then checked "Lake Tanganyika", "Lake Baikal", "Lake Michigan", and "Lake Geneva". Those checks mattered because each one landed as ordinary wording on its own, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag. The board started to behave like one phrase pattern across Tanganyika, Baikal, Michigan, Geneva, and Titicaca.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Names of lakes", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
